questions.prompt: The mice ___ killed by a cat last year. (A is, B have, C was, D with, E were)
steps: Plural mice takes were in the past passive.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Kiswahili is ___ across the continent. (A speaking, B spoken, C spoke, D speak, E now speaking)
steps: Is spoken is the passive form.

steps: Against introduces the opposing team.

questions.prompt: Answers were filled ___ pencil. (A with, B by, C for, D in, E on)

questions.prompt: A group of recruits is a ___. Bank: delegation, team, circle, batch, choir, committee, gang, panel.
steps: A batch describes recruits joining together.

questions.prompt: A group of experts is a ___.
steps: A panel comprises experts assembled for discussion or judgement.

questions.prompt: A group of singers is a ___.
steps: A choir is an organised singing group.

questions.prompt: A group of decision-makers is a ___.
steps: Committee is the bank's usual group appointed to make decisions.

questions.answer: Committee (intended); panel/team can also fit some settings.

questions.prompt: Read aloud the following poem lines in the printed order: Arts and culture / Joy to the world / The style of my arts / Creativity! / With the aroma of my talent; / Art and culture / Facing the odds of life
steps: Look at each printed word or letter carefully and say it in its printed order.
Blend sounds into words; for sentences, pause at punctuation. A teacher should assess pronunciation and fluency, rather than a different written answer.
questions.answer: Oral response: Arts and culture / Joy to the world / The style of my arts / Creativity! / With the aroma of my talent; / Art and culture / Facing the odds of life

questions.prompt: Who is speaking in the arts-and-culture poem?
steps: My arts and my talent support this interpretation; no personal name is printed.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: The poetic speaker/persona, apparently an artist or creative person.

questions.prompt: What is the poem about?
steps: Connect the arts/talent lines with the joy and final challenge line.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Arts, culture and creative talent bringing joy and helping people face life's challenges.

questions.prompt: What do arts and culture bring to the world?
steps: The second line explicitly says joy to the world.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Give a synonym of the bold word Joy.
steps: These words express the same joyful feeling.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What lesson can be learned?
steps: A supported interpretation is acceptable; explain it using the poem's ideas.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Model interpretation: Develop creative talents and value arts and culture because they bring happiness and help us face challenges.
